transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I guess what brings me in is… I took on this historical society project and acted like I could run the whole fundraiser myself. I started making quilt designs, calling volunteers, putting together schedules, promising deadlines—just a lot more than I could realistically handle.
Have you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or irritable while working on this project, like you didn’t need much sleep or couldn’t slow your thoughts down?
Yes. At first I felt really up, almost glowing, like every idea I had was a great one. But if anyone questioned me or slowed me down, I got snappish. I felt like they were just getting in my way.
Did you find yourself acting impulsively or taking risks in other areas of your life during this time, like spending sprees, reckless driving, or other unusual behaviors?

I’m not sure I’d say that. I don’t remember doing things like driving recklessly or going on big spending sprees. Mostly it was the project stuff—saying yes to too much and acting like I could handle it all.
After that initial period of feeling really up and energetic, did you experience a time when you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things for several days or more?

Yes… after that, I kind of went flat. I used to really enjoy checking on my garden and working on my own quilt entries, but lately I just look at the fabric or the seed catalogs and don’t feel much of anything.
How long did you feel that way—up, energetic, and irritable—at the beginning of this project?
It lasted longer than I realized at the time… about five months, I think. That whole overdriven stretch with the historical society project went on until things sort of fell apart.

After you started feeling down and losing interest in your garden and quilting, did you also experience other symptoms of depression like changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or thoughts of worthlessness or suicide?

Yes, mostly my sleep changed. For a while I was only sleeping a few hours, and I’d wake up feeling like I should sew or start making phone calls right away. But now it’s different… I either lie awake worrying, or I sleep late and still feel worn out.

During that time when you felt up, energetic, and irritable, did you ever feel like your mood was so high or your behavior so out of the ordinary that someone else might have noticed something unusual, even if you didn’t think anything was wrong yourself?

Yes, I think so. At first I felt almost… glowing, like every idea I had was a good one, a wonderful one even. I didn’t see it as strange then, but looking back, I’m sure people noticed. And if anyone questioned me or slowed me down, I got pretty snappish, like they were just getting in my way.
During that time when you felt up, energetic, and irritable, was there at least one full week where those feelings were present most of the day, nearly every day?
Yes. It wasn’t just a few days. That overdriven feeling was there most of the time for months—about five months, really—before everything fell apart with the project.
